procedures_covered: Implantable VAD: bridge to transplant, bridge to recovery (post-cardiotomy), destination therapy
Percutaneous VAD for cardiogenic shock / AMI / high-risk PCI
Total artificial heart as bridge to transplant

k_of_n.quote: meeting ONE of the following: On optimal medical management ... for at least 45 of the last 60 days ... OR Advanced heart failure for at least 14 days and dependent on intra-aortic balloon pump for >=7 days

logic.exclusions_or_contraindications: None listed as such; 'Other applications ... including the use of total artificial hearts as destination therapy, are considered experimental or investigational.'
logic.initial_vs_repeat: Not addressed in the statement (codes include replacement and removal, no criteria).

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Inotrope-dependent, OR cardiac index <2.2 liters/min/m2, while not on inotropes and also meeting ONE of the following:
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Destination-therapy bullets are an implicit AND list (no connector between NYHA, LVEF and this bullet), but this bullet has an inner OR and the 'ONE of' sub-list applies to one or to both of its options.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: Are currently listed as heart transplant candidates, OR Are undergoing evaluation to determine candidacy for heart transplant, AND Are not expected to survive until a donor heart can be obtained
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: OR then AND at the same level: (listed OR evaluating) AND not expected to survive.

and_or_ambiguity.quote: when both of the following are met: Device is used for temporary circulatory support for up to thirty days ... AND Member is willing and able to be treated with heparin
and_or_ambiguity.why_ambiguous: Fine, but 'willing and able' is a patient-commitment item with no objective test.

extraction_hazards: Sub-headings ('Ventricular Assist Devices', 'Total Artificial Hearts') are plain lines; 'Bridge' indications are bullets with 'o' sub-bullets and '-' third-level markers.
'OTHER' section (about 90 lines) is product-by-product FDA approvals with bullets that look like criteria; the first line says it is illustrative, 'not intended to be a recommendation'.
Description of codes in a 60-row HCPCS table with wrapped descriptions.
Reference list is ~96 items long, nearly half the file.
interesting_structures: Several device types, each with its own indication set; reuse of 'FDA-approved or cleared [including Humanitarian Device Exemption (HDE)]' as a device-status leaf.
Time ratios (45 of 60 days) and 'at least 14 days' as multi-window requirements.
Device-label detail in OTHER (e.g. pediatric BSA 0.7-1.5 m2) not in Position Statement: coverage rules and FDA labels can diverge.

fit_to_tree.why: Numeric leaves fit well, but implicit AND/OR with an inner 'ONE of', patient-intent leaf, and labelling text in OTHER create ambiguity. Device status ('FDA-approved') is a non-chart fact.
